extracted.intended_audience: aspiring storytellers, screenwriters, and creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Concise practical rules for crafting character-driven cinematic stories and general storytelling applicable to screenwriters and fiction writers. Includes 22 short, actionable maxims from a Pixar storyboard artist emphasizing structure, character, theme, and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admire character for trying
rubrics_metrics.description: You admire a character for trying more than for their successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters sympathetic through their efforts and struggles rather than only their victories; emphasize attempts and growth over flawless achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think like the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: You gotta keep in mind what's interesting to you as an audience, not what's fun to do as a writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize audience engagement and curiosity over writerly exercises or cleverness that doesn't serve interest; test scenes for audience appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme may reveal late
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying for theme is important, but you won't see what the story is actually about til you're at the end of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to discovering the true theme through the writing process; attempt to plant thematic seeds but allow the completed story to reveal its central meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple cause-effect structure template
rubrics_metrics.description: Once upon a time there was ___. Every day, ___. One day ___. Because of that, ___. Because of that, ___. Until finally ___.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this simple chain-of-events template to map motivation and causality and to ensure each event leads logically to the next toward a resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify. Focus. Combine characters. Hop over detours. You'll feel like you're losing valuable stuff but it sets you free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim subplots and characters that distract from the core story; consolidation often strengthens clarity and pace even if it feels like loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge the character's strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: What is your character good at, comfortable with? Throw the polar opposite at them. Challenge them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create conflict by forcing characters into situations that contradict their skills or comforts to provoke growth and drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design the ending early
rubrics_metrics.description: Come up with your ending before you figure out your middle. Endings are hard, get yours working up front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the destination so the story can be structured to lead there; an effective ending anchors the middle and informs choices about plot and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish and move on
rubrics_metrics.description: Finish your story, let go even if it's not perfect. In an ideal world you have both, but move on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ship work rather than endlessly refining; completed drafts can be improved later and finishing enables learning and iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'what wouldn't happen next' to get unstuck
rubrics_metrics.description: When you're stuck, make a list of what WOULDN'T happen next. Lots of times the material to get you unstuck will show up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate constraints and anti-options to reveal surprising possibilities and avoid obvious or clichéd continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze stories you like
rubrics_metrics.description: Pull apart the stories you like. What you like in them is a part of you; you've got to recognize it before you can use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deconstruct admired works to identify personal tastes and repeatable techniques you can consciously employ in your own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put ideas on paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting it on paper lets you start fixing it. If it stays in your head, a perfect idea, you'll never share it with anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Externalize ideas quickly; writing reveals flaws and opportunities and is the only way to iterate and improve a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount the obvious ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Discount the 1st thing that comes to mind. And the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th — get the obvious out of the way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push past immediate, safe choices to find more original, layered solutions; brainstorming beyond the first few ideas yields better material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give characters opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Give your characters opinions. Passive/malleable might seem likable to you as you write, but it's poison to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should express desires and judgments; decisive opinions create conflict and make characters compelling to watch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify your story's burning belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Why must you tell THIS story? What's the belief burning within you that your story feeds off of?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify your personal stake and the core conviction driving the story; this fuels authenticity and thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with emotional honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were your character, in this situation, how would you feel? Honesty lends credibility to unbelievable situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor even fantastic plots in truthful emotions and reactions to make them believable and relatable to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the stakes? Give us reason to root for the character. What happens if they don't succeed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly establish consequences and urgency so the audience cares about the outcome and invests in the character's journey.

rubrics_metrics.name: No work is wasted
rubrics_metrics.description: No work is ever wasted. If it's not working, let go and move on — it'll come back around to be useful later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandoned ideas may be repurposed; view drafts and experiments as material for future projects rather than failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the difference between testing and fussing
rubrics_metrics.description: You have to know yourself: the difference between doing your best & fussing. Story is testing, not refining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish healthy iterative experimentation from endless tinkering; focus on learning through tests rather than polishing prematurely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use coincidences carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Coincidences to get characters into trouble are great; coincidences to get them out of it are cheating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow fate or chance to create conflict plausibly, but avoid deus ex machina solutions that resolve problems without character agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rearrange disliked elements as an exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise: take the building blocks of a movie you dislike. How d'you rearrange them into what you DO like?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negative examples as creative prompts to discover fresh combinations and to clarify your taste and storytelling priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make characters/situations identifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: You gotta identify with your situation/characters, can't just write 'cool'. What would make YOU act that way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground characters' motivations in relatable impulses and believable stakes rather than surface 'cool' traits to ensure authentic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the essence of the story
rubrics_metrics.description: What's the essence of your story? Most economical telling of it? If you know that, you can build out from there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distill the core idea into its simplest, most potent form to guide decisions about structure, tone, and what to include or cut.
